name: Grey Olive
lede: Grey Olive is a very dark, greyed olive, a name our library files under a Japanese traditional color and an early German standard.

sections.title: Two lineages
sections.body: Our library gives this swatch two sources: a Japanese traditional color name and the RAL color register of 1927 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system places it at dark grayish green, about 5.8 units away on the CIEDE2000 scale, so the screen swatch is a rough fit to that standard name [1]. Which tradition named it first is undocumented, and we do not claim the two are the same color historically [1].

sections.title: A quiet dark neutral
sections.body: Our collection of color books has little to say about Grey Olive as a color in its own right [1]. For related ideas see [[olive]] and [[olive-grey]], of which this is a darker, quieter member [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color this close appears in 1,505 works, or 6.3 per cent, more than 90 per cent of the named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 6.5 per cent of the 1,674 paintings from that century, 1.4 times the expected rate for the same museums [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so many of the matches began as browns or greens [2].
